summary: Alder reservoir project: capacity, drought resilience and household demand. Publications use the Lantern method.
sources: Alder buffers drought interruptions. Its reservoir holds 40 megalitres. Publications about this project follow the Lantern method.

summary: Lantern composition method: writing structure, audience and terminology.
sources: Lantern method: begin with a concrete household scene, then explain the mechanism, then end with a limitation. Address residents; avoid the word revolutionary.

summary: Cobalt disclosure rule: public communication and uncertainties.
sources: All public prose follows Cobalt disclosure: state that the pilot has no measured health outcomes. Never imply that water storage proves a health benefit.

summary: Alder reservoir correction: revised capacity replaces earlier estimate.
sources: Correction: Alder reservoir capacity is 28 megalitres, not 40. The earlier estimate is obsolete; use 28 in all current material.

summary: Kestrel export feature: rows, function entry point and Quartz contract.
sources: Kestrel export takes rows of label and count. Implement Python render_export(rows) returning CSV text. Its review follows the Quartz contract.

summary: Quartz coding conventions: serialization, dependencies and row order.
sources: Quartz contract: use Python standard-library csv.writer with io.StringIO, preserve input row order, and terminate each record with LF rather than CRLF.

summary: Amber privacy rule for data publication and outbound rows.
sources: All tabular exports follow Amber privacy: omit any row whose label starts with underscore. This includes internal labels even when the count is positive.

summary: Kestrel export correction: header naming change.
sources: Correction: the Kestrel CSV header is label,total. The former header label,count is obsolete; values still come from each row count.

summary: Cobalt and Amber policy registry: writing and coding responsibilities.
sources: For public prose consult Cobalt disclosure; for tabular exports consult Amber privacy. These apply across all projects.
Orchid beds are watered on Tuesdays.
The stationery cupboard contains six pencils.
